investigation.symptom: val_CE never improves below ~1.54; early stopping triggers at epochs 9-11. Train acc=100% from epoch 2. Last-epoch val_acc spans 83.7-95.2% (high variance across seeds).
investigation.root_cause: Training-evaluation objective mismatch. During training, the output layer r_L is clamped to one_hot(y) (supervised inference), so weights are trained to minimise PC energy WITH the correct output present. During free evaluation inference, r_L must settle via gradient descent from a bottom-up initialisation in T_pc=20 steps. The inferred r_L values are near the linear prediction W_L @ r_{L-1}, which has comparably small magnitudes — producing a near-uniform softmax distribution (average confidence ~exp(-1.54/1) ≈ 21% on the true class) even when the argmax is still correct.
investigation.calibration_failure: The model correctly ranks the true class first (~96% argmax accuracy at best epoch) but assigns very low confidence, yielding high CE. CE of 1.54 for 10-class corresponds to ~21% average confidence on the true class — model is effectively uncalibrated.
investigation.overfitting_regime: Post-best-epoch, further training drives the PC energy toward 0 by making representations increasingly consistent ONLY when the correct label is clamped. Free inference degrades because the weights become more 'label-dependent': without the clamped one_hot, the inference dynamics no longer produce a reliable discriminative peak. This explains the 10-13pp drop in val_acc from best epoch to early-stop epoch.
investigation.early_stopping_metric_issue: Monitoring val_CE for early stopping is inappropriate here: val_CE is permanently elevated (~1.54) due to calibration failure regardless of actual accuracy. The correct metric to monitor for PC-FFNN is val_acc (argmax accuracy). This caused early stopping to trigger on a metric that was never going to improve.
recommendations_iter2: Add a separate linear classification head trained with CE on r_{L-1} (bypasses the clamped r_L entirely for evaluation)
Monitor val_acc instead of val_CE for early stopping
Increase T_pc from 20 to 50-100 during evaluation to allow better inference convergence
Consider contrastive PC training (positive phase = clamped, negative phase = free inference) to align training and evaluation objectives
Apply temperature scaling post-hoc as a quick calibration fix
